name: Workflow 8 - Weedlaw Email → PDF Parse → Court Response Draft

nodes.name: Gmail: Watch for PDF Attachments
nodes.notes: Polls docweedlaw@gmail.com every minute for unread emails with PDF attachments. Credentials: attach Derek's Gmail OAuth2 credential. The filter `has:attachment filename:pdf` limits to PDFs only — ignores promotional/non-court emails.

nodes.name: Extract PDF Text
nodes.notes: Uses n8n's built-in PDF extraction (no external API needed). Outputs the raw text content of the first PDF attachment. If multiple attachments exist, add a Loop node upstream to process each — for now assumes single-attachment emails.

nodes.name: Parse: Extract Case Metadata
nodes.notes: Lightweight client-side parsing — no API cost. Extracts doc type, hearing date, and court file number from the raw text using regex patterns tuned for Ontario Superior Court document formats. Expand patterns here as new document types are encountered.

values.content: You are a legal document assistant for a self-represented litigant in Ontario, Canada. You help draft court response templates based on incoming documents. Always include: (1) proper Ontario Superior Court header format, (2) court file number, (3) responding party section, (4) grounds for the response, (5) order sought, (6) a note that this is a draft for review by a licensed paralegal or lawyer before filing. Never give legal advice — only structural drafting assistance.

=A court document has been received. Document type: {{ $json.documentType }}. Court file number: {{ $json.courtFileNumber }}. Hearing date: {{ $json.hearingDate }}.

Document text (first 3000 characters):
{{ $json.rawText.substring(0, 3000) }}

Please draft a response template to this {{ $json.documentType }} in proper Ontario Superior Court format. Include all required sections. Mark any section requiring Derek's specific facts as [INSERT: description].

nodes.name: AI: Draft Court Response
nodes.notes: Uses OpenAI gpt-4o-mini (cost-efficient for structured drafting). Credential: attach Derek's OpenAI API key. Temperature 0.3 keeps output deterministic and structured. To switch to Claude (preferred for legal), replace node type with n8n-nodes-base.anthropic, model claude-3-5-haiku-20241022, same message structure — Claude follows Ontario court formatting instructions more reliably.

nodes.name: Save Draft to Supabase
nodes.notes: Saves the draft to the `court_responses` Supabase table. Create this table: court_responses(id uuid PK, source_email text, email_subject text, document_type text, court_file_number text, hearing_date text, draft_response text, status text, created_at timestamptz default now()). Uses the same Supabase credential as Workflows 2 and 7.

nodes.name: Email Draft to Derek
nodes.notes: Sends the draft back to docweedlaw@gmail.com so Derek can review it directly in his inbox. Subject includes court file number for easy filtering. Same Gmail credential as the trigger node.

notes:
SETUP CHECKLIST (all one-time actions Derek must do in n8n UI before activating):
1. Import this JSON into n8n (Settings → Import Workflow)
2. Attach Gmail OAuth2 credential to both Gmail nodes (same credential)
3. Attach OpenAI API key credential to 'AI: Draft Court Response' node — OR swap to Anthropic node (see node notes)
4. Attach Supabase credential to 'Save Draft to Supabase' node
5. Create the court_responses table in Supabase (SQL in node notes above)
6. Activate the workflow — it will poll docweedlaw@gmail.com every minute for new PDFs
